msg: No operator e-mail address. 312.4(d)(1) makes the online notice carry the name, postal address, telephone number and e-mail of the operator collecting from children.
No postal address. A support e-mail alone does not satisfy 312.4(d)(1); a parent must be able to write to you on paper.
No telephone number. 312.4(d)(1) lists the telephone number as its own required contact item.

The notice never says whether other operators also collect from the child. The Rule lets one operator be named as the contact only if the notice still lists all operators collecting through the service.
The notice does not say whether information is collected directly from the child or passively. 312.4(d)(2) requires both to be distinguished.
Third parties are mentioned but neither their identities nor their categories and purposes are given. The amended Rule closed the 'we may share with third parties' shortcut.

Missing the separate-consent statement: a parent must be able to consent to collection and use without also consenting to disclosure to third parties. This is the single most common gap in notices written before 2026.
No retention section. 312.10 requires a written retention policy for children's personal information, published in this notice.
Retention is mentioned but no timeframe is given. 312.10 wants the purposes, the timeframe, and the deletion commitment - not just the word 'retention'.
when: retention polic|how long we (keep|retain|store)|data retention|we retain

msg: Indefinite retention of children's data is prohibited outright by 312.10. Remove this sentence and give a timeframe.
pats: for as long as (we|the company)[^.]{0,30}(deem|wish|choose|see fit)

msg: The notice never states the deletion commitment - that children's data is deleted once it is no longer needed for the purpose it was collected for, and is not retained indefinitely.
Parental rights are incomplete. The notice must state all three: review the child's information, delete it, and refuse any further collection - plus the procedure for each.
Persistent identifiers, cookies or analytics are described without the support-for-internal-operations basis. Without that phrase the collection needs verifiable parental consent instead.
The notice never states that you do not condition a child's participation on disclosing more information than is reasonably necessary. 312.7 is a standing prohibition and parents look for it.
COPPA's threshold is under 13. This notice never states it - a notice built around 16 or 18 is a GDPR or state-law notice, not a COPPA notice.
Wrong compliance date for the amended COPPA Rule. The Rule was published 22 January 2025 and effective 23 June 2025, but full compliance was required from 22 April 2026.

A school or classroom context is described but the school-authorization limits are not. The amended Rule allows school authorisation only where the data is used for the educational purpose and for no commercial purpose.
